payload.name: decimation

payload.name: pre-ringing

payload.body: Pre-ringing is a human-made signal processing artifact where a filtered signal exhibits transient overshoot or oscillation before a sudden step change or impulse. Parameters: filter type (linear-phase FIR, linear-phase IIR), filter order, cutoff frequency, and the signal's step edge characteristics. Mechanism: symmetric impulse response of linear-phase filters spreads filter energy equally before and after the impulse, causing perceptible pre-ringing on sharp transients. Persistence mechanism: inherent property of linear-phase filter implementations; documented in DSP literature; perceptually significant in audio processing where pre-ringing is more objectionable than post-ringing. payload.body: Audio compression is the technique of reducing the dynamic range of an audio signal by attenuating loudest passages and/or amplifying quietest ones. Parameters: threshold (the amplitude level above which compression engages), compression ratio (the degree of attenuation applied above threshold), attack time (how quickly compression engages after threshold is exceeded), release time (how quickly compression disengages after signal falls below threshold), and knee (the transition shape around threshold). Persistence mechanism: implemented as a configurable algorithm in digital audio workstations, hardware compressors, streaming codecs, and broadcast chains, where it processes audio samples in real-time or offline. The technique is defined by its control parameters and their interaction with signal amplitude over time, persisting through software implementations, hardware circuits, and standardized codec specifications. [formal: compressio-audio | substrate: matter | horizon: a moment | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

Anti-aliasing is the technique of removing or attenuating frequency components above the Nyquist frequency (half the sampling rate) before sampling, to prevent those high-frequency components from being misinterpreted as lower-frequency aliases in the sampled signal. Parameters: cutoff frequency (the frequency at which attenuation begins), filter order (the steepness of the rolloff), and rolloff rate (dB/octave attenuation above cutoff). Persistence mechanism: implemented as analog low-pass filters in analog-to-digital converters, as digital interpolation filters in sample-rate converters, and as algorithmic oversampling in digital-to-analog converters. The technique is defined by its cutoff characteristics relative to the sampling rate and persists through hardware filter designs, DSP algorithms, and sampling-theory standards. [formal: anti-aliasing | substrate: matter | horizon: a moment | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]
